newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND WANTS EURO FIX PRINCIPLES SOONEST POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND WANTS EURO FIX PRINCIPLES SOONEST POSSIBLE.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Thursday principles guiding the conversion of national currencies into the new euro should be decided as early as possible.
He said the markka's central parity rate in Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) would be about the right level for Finland to fix the markka to the euro.

"I would like to see that the final rate would be fixed as soon as possible, at least how we are going to decide when the time comes. So...decisions about the principles should be done as early as possible," Niinisto said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) due for broadcast later on Thursday.
"We have an ERM central rate, and I think it is approximately the correct one for us," he said.
The markka's ERM central parity rate is 3.04 per German mark. The markka joined the ERM in October 1996 and has since been mostly trading above the midpoint.
Niinisto said it was equally important that countries intending to join the single currency fulfilled the entry criteria and that the third phase of EMU started on time.
There would be "no damage done" if EMU were to start with a broad membership as long as Finland's stance that participants lived up to the standards was adhered to, he said.
"Finland meets (the criteria), and why we meet the criteria is because we have political will to meet the criteria to (beef up) the state economy," he said.
"I believe that others will do their job properly, too," he added.
